page.title: SAML 2.0
page.subtitle: Federate McHarbor login to any SAML 2.0 identity provider (Okta, Auth0, Keycloak, ADFS, Google Workspace, Azure AD, etc.). The plugin handles the SP side: building the ServiceProvider, generating signed AuthnRequests, and parsing signed assertions at the ACS endpoint.
page.registerHint: Add a provider from the host's Settings > Security > Identity Providers page and pick "SAML 2.0" as the provider_type.

help.metadata_url: URL of the IdP's SAML 2.0 metadata XML document. The plugin fetches this on every login to discover the IdP's SSO endpoint and signing certificate. The URL must be reachable from McHarbor without authentication.
help.entity_id: Optional SP entity ID advertised in the SP metadata. Leave empty to use the McHarbor metadata URL. The value must match what's configured on the IdP side or sign-in will fail with "Unknown SP".
help.sp_certificate: Optional PEM-encoded X.509 certificate for the SP. Required only if the IdP expects signed AuthnRequests or encrypted assertions. Generate with `openssl req -x509 -newkey rsa:2048 -keyout sp.key -out sp.crt -days 365 -nodes -subj '/CN=mcharbor'`. Stored encrypted at rest.
help.sp_private_key: Optional PEM-encoded RSA private key matching the SP certificate. PKCS#1 (`-----BEGIN RSA PRIVATE KEY-----`) and PKCS#8 (`-----BEGIN PRIVATE KEY-----`) are both accepted. Stored encrypted at rest.

guide.title: Set up SAML 2.0 sign-in in McHarbor
guide.subtitle: Point your IdP at the McHarbor metadata URL, paste the IdP metadata URL into McHarbor, and optionally upload a keypair for signed AuthnRequests.

step1.title: Locate your IdP's SAML metadata URL
step1.body: Every IdP exposes a SAML 2.0 metadata XML document describing its SSO endpoint and signing certificate. Common locations: Okta > Applications > your app > Sign On > Settings > Metadata URL; Auth0 > Application > Addons > SAML2 > Usage > Identity Provider Metadata; Keycloak > Realm > Endpoints > SAML 2.0 Identity Provider Metadata. Copy the URL into the IdP Metadata URL field on the provider form.

step2.title: Download the McHarbor SP metadata
step2.body: Click "Download SP metadata" on the provider edit page (or GET /api/identity-providers/<id>/metadata). The XML includes the McHarbor ACS URL and (if you uploaded a keypair) the SP signing certificate. Upload this file or paste its contents into your IdP's "Import SP metadata" or "New SAML application" wizard.

step3.title: Set the ACS URL on the IdP side
step3.body: If your IdP requires manual entry instead of metadata import, set the Assertion Consumer Service URL to `<mcharbor-base>/api/identity-providers/callback` and the SP Entity ID to the value shown on the provider form (default: `<mcharbor-base>/api/identity-providers/metadata`). The NameID format should be `EmailAddress` or `Unspecified`.

step4.title: (Optional) Upload a SP keypair for signed requests
step4.body: If your IdP requires signed AuthnRequests, generate a self-signed RSA keypair: `openssl req -x509 -newkey rsa:2048 -keyout sp.key -out sp.crt -days 365 -nodes -subj '/CN=mcharbor'`. Paste the entire contents of sp.crt into the SP Certificate field and sp.key into the SP Private Key field. Re-download the SP metadata and re-upload to the IdP so it picks up the new signing certificate.

step5.title: Map IdP attributes to McHarbor claims
step5.body: On the IdP side, ensure the assertion includes at minimum an email attribute (urn:oid:0.9.2342.19200300.100.1.3 or http://schemas.xmlsoap.org/ws/2005/05/identity/claims/emailaddress). Display name is optional. Group membership is read from `http://schemas.microsoft.com/ws/2008/06/identity/claims/groups` if present, but no admin-group fetch API is wired in v1.

step6.title: Test the connection
step6.body: Back in McHarbor, click "Test connection" on the provider form. A green result means the IdP metadata URL resolved and parsed correctly. Click "Sign in with SAML" on the login page to verify the full flow — you should land back in McHarbor with a session cookie.
